title:
The Death of the
Rice Farmer
description: Birds keep eating a farmer's rice. He lies still in his field and uses a surprising trick to protect his harvest.

source.adaptation: Original Hypa retelling of the documented folktale; see SOURCES.md.

lines.text: A rice farmer worked hard in his field, hoping to gather a good harvest.
But birds kept coming to eat the rice he had grown.
He guarded the field, yet the birds returned whenever they could.
The farmer decided to use a trick instead of chasing them again.
He killed an animal and laid its entrails across his own belly.
Then he lay down in the field and pretended to be dead.
ask: Why does the farmer pretend to be dead?

lines.text: The birds watched the still figure among the rice.
Believing he was dead, the birds came close.
When they were within reach, he sprang up and caught them.
ask: How does the farmer protect his field?

lines.text: After that, his rice field was safe from those birds.
The title speaks of the farmer's death, but he had only pretended.
The lesson is that careful thought can solve a problem that chasing alone cannot.
That is how the rice farmer protected the harvest he had worked for.
